messages.subject: How to transform JSON object columns in tbl to tbl with single values from json
messages.subject_clean: How to transform JSON object columns in tbl to tbl with single values from json
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

i successfully connected to CrateDB and generate a tbl object:

devtools::install_github("tidyverse/dbplyr")
devtools::install_github("tidyverse/dplyr")
library(dplyr)
library(dbplyr)

crateTable <- "raw"

### Import via DB ¸
drv <- JDBC("io.crate.client.jdbc.CrateDriver","/home/rstudio/projects/jdbc/crate-jdbc-standalone-2.1.6.jar")
conn <- dbConnect(drv, "jdbc:crate://c02.demo.cratedb.cloud:5432/rstudio")
dbListTables(conn)

#Data Frame
rawTbl <- tbl(conn,crateTable)
head(rawTbl)

However, CrateDB supports Object Columns which are output as JSON through the JDBC Driver:

> head(rawTbl)
Source:     lazy query [?? x 6]
Database:   JDBCConnection

# S3: tbl_dbi
                                f_article                                                                                         f_metric                     g_month_ts  name
                                    <chr>                                                                                            <chr>                          <chr> <chr>
1 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362}          {"name":"Weight.Cav4.act.g","description":"Weight.Cav4.act.g","value":-0.48,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
2 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362}                      {"name":"CycleTime","description":"CycleTime","value":10.551185,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
3 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362} {"name":"E1.Spd.act.rev_min","description":"E1.Spd.act.rev_min","value":0.0060422616,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
4 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362}                        {"name":"BlowingTime","description":"BlowingTime","value":7.0,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
5 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362}                        {"name":"CavityCount","description":"CavityCount","value":5.0,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
6 {"name":"$Abmusterung PE/PP","id":3362}           {"name":"Weight.Cav3.act.g","description":"Weight.Cav3.act.g","value":0.51,"status":0} 2017-03-01 00:00:00.000 +00 AD power
# ... with 2 more variables: tags <chr>, ts <chr>

How can I now transform the dataframe with json objects for instance to a new table which only displays certain values from the json objects, for instance (pseudocode):

newTbl <- select(rawTbl, f_article['name'], f_article['id'], ts, f_metric['description'])

with lazy loading?

Its a table with 30Mio Records and should grow larger.

Thanks a lot,

Michael

messages.subject: Problem using httr with OAuth 1.0 api site
messages.subject_clean: Problem using httr with OAuth 1.0 api site
messages.body_plain:
I would like to use httr with an OAuth 1.0 api.

I've already registered, generated credentials (keys, tokens), but I'm having a difficult time implementing this through httr.

Under the api instructions, it says that each http request is to include a "well-formed OAuth header", with the following provided example:

Authorization: OAuth
  oauth_consumer_key="0685bd9184jfhq22",
  oauth_token="ad180jjd733klru7",
  oauth_signature_method="HMAC-SHA1",
  oauth_signature="wOJIO9A2W5mFwDgiDvZbTSMK%2FPY%3D",
  oauth_timestamp="137131200",
  oauth_nonce="4572616e48616d6d65724c61686176",
  oauth_version="1.0"

my httr attempt (using my own credentials, of course) is as approximately as follows:

GET("https://api.endpoint/v1/data.xml",
  query = list(symbols = "get_this"),

  add_headers(
     oauth_consumer_key="0685bd9184jfhq22",
     oauth_token="ad180jjd733klru7",
     oauth_signature_method="HMAC-SHA1",
     oauth_version="1.0"
 ))

This gives a 401 status code.

It's unclear how I'm to comply with the indicated header schema; any guidance is appreciated.

Again, thanks to anyone for any guidance.

rawTbl %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate_all(jsonlite::fromJSON)

Then use purrr and techniques from https://jennybc.github.io/purrr-tutorial/

messages.subject: Help programming function using dplyr and the _ versions of commands
messages.subject_clean: Help programming function using dplyr and the _ versions of commands
messages.body_plain:
The point of the function in the MWE program below is to start with a dataframe with variables z,x1,x2,and y and to generate a new dataframe that is ordered by z and contains z, the first difference of x1, the first difference of x2, and the first difference of y.

I'm confused by the referencing and dereferencing rules in dplyr, the underscore versions of the basic dplyr functions, e.g., mutate_, and why assignments don't seem to work normally but apparently need I().

The code below sort of works, but I can't figure out how to name the transformation of the individual x variables (I'm planning to do this with many variables, not just x1 and x2).  The program currently overwrites the previous x variable each time the loop runs. Also, although I use the "~" and as.name <http://as.name/>() constructions that are recommended by some of the web pages on programming with dplyr, I don't really understand what I'm doing.  I also suspect that although the ~I() construction works, it is considered inelegant compared to what I'm supposed to be doing.

Comments or suggestions welcome. I've been working as best I can from, for example, http://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/programming.html

Thank you.

Yours,
Michael

(my.D = data.frame(my.y=runif(10), my.x1=runif(10), my.x2=1:10, my.z=runif(10)))

my.plm  <- function(D,y,x,z) {
    require(dplyr)
    require(lazyeval)
    z  <- as.name <http://as.name/>(z)
    y  <- as.name <http://as.name/>(y)
    print(D  <- arrange_(D,z))
    print(summarize_( D,~mean(z),~mean(y) ))
    print(D.fd  <- mutate_(D,
                     z = z,
                     y = ~I(y - lag(y,n=1L))
               )
          )
    for(xvar in x) {
        print(varname  <- paste("x_", xvar, sep=""))
        xvar  <- as.name <http://as.name/>(xvar)
        print(D.fd  <- mutate_(D.fd,
                           ~I(xvar - lag(xvar,n=1L))
                           )
              )
    }
}

my.plm(D=my.D,y="my.y",x=c("my.x1","my.x2"),z="my.z")
